African.name: African
African.description: Rich and diverse culinary traditions from across the African continent.

berbere.name: Berbere
berbere.description: Ethiopian hot spice blend made from chili peppers, garlic, ginger and various spices
berbere.preparationNotes: Traditionally dry-roasted and ground by hand, though now commercial versions are widely available.
berbere.technicalTips: Toast the spices before grinding for maximum flavor development.

harissa.name: Harissa
harissa.description: North African hot chili pepper paste with garlic, olive oil and spices
harissa.preparationNotes: Can be preserved in olive oil for months when refrigerated.
harissa.technicalTips: For milder harissa, remove seeds from peppers before processing.

duqqa.name: Duqqa
duqqa.description: Egyptian dry spice blend with nuts, herbs, and spices
duqqa.preparationNotes: Each family has their own recipe - proportions vary significantly.
duqqa.technicalTips: Allow to cool completely before storing to maintain crunch.

chermoula.name: Chermoula
chermoula.description: A vibrant Moroccan marinade and sauce made with fresh herbs, aromatic spices, lemon, and olive oil - widely used in North African cuisine
chermoula.preparationNotes: Traditionally prepared by hand-grinding all ingredients in a mortar and pestle to release maximum flavor. Best made fresh, but can be stored for up to a week refrigerated.
chermoula.technicalTips: Balance acidity with enough olive oil for a smooth emulsion. For best results, allow flavors to marry for at least 30 minutes before using.

peanut.name: West African Peanut Sauce
peanut.description: Rich, creamy sauce made from ground peanuts, tomatoes, and spices
peanut.preparationNotes: The sauce thickens significantly as it cools.
peanut.technicalTips: Roast raw peanuts before grinding for deeper flavor.

regionalCuisines.name: North African Cuisine
regionalCuisines.description: Mediterranean and Arabic influenced cuisine featuring tagines, couscous, and aromatic spices

regionalCuisines.name: West African Cuisine
regionalCuisines.description: Bold, spicy cuisine with staples like rice, cassava, plantains and palm oil

regionalCuisines.name: East African Cuisine
regionalCuisines.description: Diverse cuisine influenced by Arabic, Indian and indigenous traditions

regionalCuisines.name: Southern African Cuisine
regionalCuisines.description: Hearty cuisine combining indigenous, Dutch, Malaysian and British influences

American.name: American
American.description: Diverse culinary influences reflecting the melting pot of American culture.

bbqSauce.name: BBQ Sauce
bbqSauce.description: Sweet, tangy, and smoky tomato-based sauce for grilled and smoked meats
bbqSauce.preparationNotes: Traditionally simmered slowly to develop deep flavor and thicken
bbqSauce.technicalTips: Balance acid, sweetness, and spice to complement the meat it will accompany

ranchDressing.name: Ranch Dressing
ranchDressing.description: Creamy, herb-flecked dressing with buttermilk and garlic notes
ranchDressing.preparationNotes: Best when made fresh and allowed to rest for flavors to meld
ranchDressing.technicalTips: Use fresh herbs when possible for brightest flavor

frenchOnionDip.name: French Onion Dip
frenchOnionDip.description: Classic American tavern and party dip of slow-caramelized onions folded into tangy sour cream and mayonnaise
frenchOnionDip.preparationNotes: Cool caramelized onions completely before folding into dairy to prevent thermal splitting
frenchOnionDip.technicalTips: Refrigerate for at least 2 hours before serving for flavor infusion and ideal dip viscosity

hotSauce.name: Hot Sauce
hotSauce.description: Fiery, vinegar-based sauce with chili peppers for heat
hotSauce.preparationNotes: Can be fermented for complex flavor or used fresh for bright heat
hotSauce.technicalTips: Control heat level by adjusting pepper types and quantity

gravySauce.name: Gravy
gravySauce.description: Rich, savory sauce made from meat drippings and thickened with flour
gravySauce.preparationNotes: Must be made while cooking protein for authentic flavor from drippings
gravySauce.technicalTips: Use a whisk to prevent lumps and incorporate flour smoothly

mapleGlaze.name: Maple Glaze
mapleGlaze.description: Sweet and rich syrup reduction for breakfast items and desserts
mapleGlaze.preparationNotes: Grade B maple syrup offers more robust flavor for cooking
mapleGlaze.technicalTips: Reduce slowly to prevent burning the sugars

regionalCuisines.name: Southern Cuisine
regionalCuisines.description: Soul-warming food with African, European and Native American influences

regionalCuisines.name: New England Cuisine
regionalCuisines.description: Seafood-forward cuisine with British colonial roots and seasonal emphasis

regionalCuisines.name: Southwestern Cuisine
regionalCuisines.description: Bold flavors influenced by Mexican, Spanish, and Native American traditions

regionalCuisines.name: Midwestern Cuisine
regionalCuisines.description: Hearty comfort food emphasizing locally grown ingredients and German influence

regionalCuisines.name: California Cuisine
regionalCuisines.description: Fresh, produce-forward cooking with Mediterranean and Asian influences

Chinese.name: Chinese
Chinese.description: Ancient culinary traditions with a focus on balance and wok hei.

soy.name: Soy Sauce
soy.description: Fermented soybean sauce that forms the foundation of Chinese cooking
soy.preparationNotes: Traditionally fermented for months or years to develop complexity
soy.technicalTips: Use light soy for flavor, dark soy for color and deeper notes

hoisin.name: Hoisin Sauce
hoisin.description: Sweet and savory sauce with a thick consistency
hoisin.preparationNotes: Balance of sweet and savory can vary by region and brand
hoisin.technicalTips: Thin with water or rice wine for a lighter glaze

xo.name: XO Sauce
xo.description: Luxury seafood sauce with deep umami flavors
xo.preparationNotes: Traditionally requires expensive ingredients and significant preparation time
xo.technicalTips: A little goes a long way - use sparingly to add depth

black_bean.name: Black Bean Sauce
black_bean.description: Savory sauce made from fermented black soybeans
black_bean.preparationNotes: Beans are typically rinsed before use to moderate saltiness
black_bean.technicalTips: Mash beans slightly to release more flavor when cooking

oyster.name: Oyster Sauce
oyster.description: Rich, savory sauce with sweet undertones made from oyster extracts
oyster.preparationNotes: Modern versions are thickened with cornstarch
oyster.technicalTips: Add at the end of cooking to preserve flavor complexity

regionalCuisines.name: Cantonese Cuisine
regionalCuisines.description: Light, fresh flavors that highlight natural tastes of ingredients, with an emphasis on steaming and stir-frying

regionalCuisines.name: Sichuan Cuisine
regionalCuisines.description: Bold, spicy flavors featuring Sichuan peppercorns' numbing sensation (málà) and complex layering of flavors

regionalCuisines.name: Shandong Cuisine
regionalCuisines.description: One of China's oldest cuisines, featuring fresh seafood, quick frying, and clear soups

regionalCuisines.name: Jiangsu Cuisine
regionalCuisines.description: Refined, artistically presented cuisine emphasizing seasonal ingredients and precise cutting techniques

French.name: French
French.description: Classical techniques and a focus on high-quality ingredients and sauces.

bechamel.name: Béchamel
bechamel.description: A white sauce made from milk thickened with a white roux
bechamel.preparationNotes: Heat should be gentle to prevent scorching. Whisk constantly when adding milk to prevent lumps.
bechamel.technicalTips: For a smoother sauce, heat the milk before adding it to the roux.
bechamel.storageInstructions: Refrigerate up to 3 days, cover surface with plastic wrap to prevent skin formation

veloute.name: Velouté
veloute.description: A light stock-based sauce thickened with a blonde roux
veloute.preparationNotes: The stock must be relatively clear and the roux cooked to a blonde stage.
veloute.technicalTips: Choose the stock type based on the protein it will accompany.
veloute.storageInstructions: Refrigerate up to 2 days, reheat gently while whisking

espagnole.name: Espagnole (Brown Sauce)
espagnole.description: A brown stock-based sauce thickened with a brown roux
espagnole.preparationNotes: The roux must be browned correctly to develop the deep color and flavor.
espagnole.technicalTips: Skim regularly during simmering to achieve clarity.
espagnole.storageInstructions: Refrigerate up to 4 days, freeze up to 3 months

hollandaise.name: Hollandaise
hollandaise.description: An emulsion of butter and lemon juice using egg yolks as the emulsifier
hollandaise.preparationNotes: Temperature control is critical to prevent curdling or breaking.
hollandaise.technicalTips: Use a double boiler or bain-marie and add butter gradually.
hollandaise.storageInstructions: Best served immediately, can hold warm for up to 1 hour in bain-marie

tomato.name: Tomato Sauce
tomato.description: A sauce based on tomatoes, with aromatic vegetables and stock
tomato.preparationNotes: Can be smooth or chunky depending on the preparation method.
tomato.technicalTips: For a deeper flavor, roast the tomatoes beforehand.
tomato.storageInstructions: Refrigerate up to 5 days, freeze up to 6 months

regionalCuisines.name: Provençal Cuisine
regionalCuisines.description: Mediterranean-influenced cuisine from Southern France, featuring olive oil, herbs, tomatoes, and seafood

regionalCuisines.name: Norman Cuisine
regionalCuisines.description: Butter and cream-based cuisine from Northern France, featuring apples, dairy, and seafood
signature: tripes à la mode de Caen

regionalCuisines.name: Burgundian Cuisine
regionalCuisines.description: Wine-centric cuisine known for slow-cooked dishes, mustard, and escargot

regionalCuisines.name: Alsatian Cuisine
regionalCuisines.description: German-influenced cuisine featuring charcuterie, sauerkraut, and white wines

astrologicalInfluences: Venus - Governs the sensual, pleasure-seeking aspects of French cuisine
Jupiter - Influences the celebratory and abundant nature of French dining
Mercury - Shapes the precise techniques and articulate presentation

Greek.name: Greek
Greek.description: Mediterranean flavors with fresh herbs, olive oil, and seafood.

tzatziki.name: Tzatziki
tzatziki.description: Cooling yogurt and cucumber sauce with garlic and herbs
tzatziki.preparationNotes: Properly draining the cucumber is key to a thick consistency
tzatziki.technicalTips: Salt and drain cucumbers for at least 30 minutes before mixing

avgolemono.name: Avgolemono
avgolemono.description: Silky egg and lemon sauce that thickens soups and stews
avgolemono.preparationNotes: The key is to temper the eggs properly to avoid curdling
avgolemono.technicalTips: Add hot broth to eggs very slowly while whisking constantly

ladolemono.name: Ladolemono
ladolemono.description: Simple but powerful emulsion of olive oil and lemon juice
ladolemono.preparationNotes: The ratio is typically 3 parts oil to 1 part lemon juice
ladolemono.technicalTips: Whisk vigorously or blend for proper emulsification

skordalia.name: Skordalia
skordalia.description: Pungent garlic sauce made with potato, bread, or nuts
skordalia.preparationNotes: Achieving the right balance of garlic is crucial - adjust to taste
skordalia.technicalTips: Slowly incorporate oil while blending for proper emulsification

htipiti.name: Htipiti
htipiti.description: Spicy roasted red pepper and feta dip
htipiti.preparationNotes: The smokiness of the peppers is essential for authentic flavor
htipiti.technicalTips: Roast peppers directly over flame for best smoky taste

regionalCuisines.name: Cretan Cuisine
regionalCuisines.description: Focused on local ingredients, wild greens, olive oil, and rustic preparation methods

regionalCuisines.name: Macedonian Cuisine
regionalCuisines.description: Northern Greek cuisine with strong Balkan influences and hearty dishes

regionalCuisines.name: Cycladic Cuisine
regionalCuisines.description: Island cuisine featuring seafood, local cheeses, and sun-dried ingredients

regionalCuisines.name: Peloponnesian Cuisine
regionalCuisines.description: Rich in olive oil, citrus, and slow-cooked meat and bean dishes

Indian.name: Indian
Indian.description: Complex spice blends and traditional cooking methods like the tandoor.

tandoori.name: Tandoori Marinade
tandoori.description: Yogurt-based marinade with vibrant spices for traditional tandoor cooking
tandoori.preparationNotes: Allow marination for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight for best flavor
tandoori.technicalTips: For authentic color, use Kashmiri chili powder which adds color without excess heat

tikka_masala.name: Tikka Masala
tikka_masala.description: Rich tomato-based curry sauce with cream and aromatic spices
tikka_masala.preparationNotes: Allow the sauce to simmer gently to develop complex flavors
tikka_masala.technicalTips: Add kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves) at the end for authentic aroma

raita.name: Raita
raita.description: Cooling yogurt condiment with vegetables and spices
raita.preparationNotes: Use thick, strained yogurt for best texture
raita.technicalTips: Salt and drain cucumber to prevent watery raita

tamarind_chutney.name: Tamarind Chutney
tamarind_chutney.description: Sweet and sour condiment made from tamarind pulp, jaggery and spices
tamarind_chutney.preparationNotes: Balance sweet, sour, and spicy elements carefully

coriander_mint_chutney.name: Coriander-Mint Chutney
coriander_mint_chutney.description: Fresh, vibrant green chutney with herbs and green chilies
coriander_mint_chutney.preparationNotes: Use ice water when blending to maintain bright green color
coriander_mint_chutney.technicalTips: Add a small amount of yogurt for creamier texture and longer shelf life

coconut_curry.name: Coconut Curry Sauce
coconut_curry.description: Creamy, aromatic sauce with coconut milk and south Indian spices
coconut_curry.preparationNotes: Temper spices properly to release their flavors into the coconut milk
coconut_curry.technicalTips: Use full-fat coconut milk for richness, light coconut milk may separate

onion_tomato_masala.name: Onion-Tomato Masala
onion_tomato_masala.description: Foundational sauce of caramelized onions and tomatoes for North Indian curries
onion_tomato_masala.preparationNotes: Properly caramelizing onions (bhunao) is the key to depth of flavor
onion_tomato_masala.technicalTips: Prepare in large batches and freeze in portions for quick weeknight cooking

regionalCuisines.name: Punjabi Cuisine
regionalCuisines.description: Hearty, rich cuisine with generous use of dairy, robust spices, and tandoor cooking

regionalCuisines.name: Bengali Cuisine
regionalCuisines.description: Delicate flavors with emphasis on fish, mustard, panch phoron spice blend and sweets

regionalCuisines.name: South Indian Cuisine
regionalCuisines.description: Predominantly rice-based with coconut, curry leaves, tamarind and complex spice blends

regionalCuisines.name: Gujarati Cuisine
regionalCuisines.description: Vegetarian cuisine with balance of sweet, salty and spicy flavors

Italian.name: Italian
Italian.description: Regional specialties with a focus on fresh pasta, tomatoes, and olive oil.

marinaraBase.name: Marinara Base
marinaraBase.description: Simple tomato sauce that forms the foundation of many Italian dishes
marinaraBase.preparationNotes: Best when made with San Marzano tomatoes for authentic flavor
marinaraBase.technicalTips: Simmer gently to maintain brightness of flavor
marinaraBase.storageInstructions: Store in airtight container for up to 5 days in refrigerator

besciamella.name: Besciamella
besciamella.description: Italian white sauce made from roux and milk
besciamella.preparationNotes: For silky texture, add hot milk to roux gradually while whisking constantly
besciamella.technicalTips: Infuse milk with bay leaf, onion, and clove before making sauce for depth of flavor
besciamella.storageInstructions: Store refrigerated in airtight container for up to 3 days

marinara.name: Marinara
marinara.description: Simple tomato sauce with garlic, olive oil and herbs
marinara.preparationNotes: Best when made with San Marzano tomatoes for authentic flavor
marinara.technicalTips: Simmer gently to maintain brightness of flavor

pesto.name: Pesto alla Genovese
pesto.description: Fresh basil sauce with pine nuts, garlic, Parmesan and olive oil
pesto.preparationNotes: Traditionally made in a marble mortar with wooden pestle
pesto.technicalTips: Blanch basil briefly to preserve color if making ahead

carbonara.name: Carbonara
carbonara.description: Silky sauce of eggs, hard cheese, cured pork and black pepper
variants: Lighter carbonara with less egg yolks
carbonara.preparationNotes: Never add cream - authentic carbonara is creamy from eggs alone
carbonara.technicalTips: Temper eggs carefully to prevent scrambling, use pasta water to adjust consistency

ragu.name: Ragù alla Bolognese
ragu.description: Rich, slow-cooked meat sauce from Bologna
ragu.preparationNotes: True Bolognese takes hours of gentle simmering for depth of flavor
ragu.technicalTips: Add milk toward the end of cooking for authentic richness and tenderness

bechamel.name: Besciamella
bechamel.description: Classic white sauce made from roux and milk
bechamel.preparationNotes: For silky texture, add hot milk to roux gradually while whisking constantly
bechamel.technicalTips: Infuse milk with bay leaf, onion, and clove before making sauce for depth of flavor

regionalCuisines.name: Sicilian Cuisine
regionalCuisines.description: Bold flavors reflecting diverse cultural influences with emphasis on seafood, citrus, and Arab-influenced sweets

regionalCuisines.name: Tuscan Cuisine
regionalCuisines.description: Rustic simplicity focusing on high-quality ingredients with an emphasis on beans, bread, and olive oil

regionalCuisines.name: Emilian Cuisine
regionalCuisines.description: Rich, indulgent cuisine from Italy's food valley, known for pasta, cured meats, and aged cheeses

regionalCuisines.name: Neapolitan Cuisine
regionalCuisines.description: Vibrant and tomato-forward cuisine with iconic pizza, pasta, and seafood dishes

astrologicalInfluences: Venus - Roman goddess of love and beauty influences the sensory pleasures of Italian cuisine
Jupiter - Brings abundance and generosity to communal Italian dining traditions
Mercury - Governs the communication and conviviality central to Italian food culture

Japanese.name: Japanese
Japanese.description: Precision and seasonality with a focus on umami and fresh seafood.

dashi.name: Dashi
dashi.description: Fundamental Japanese stock that serves as the base for many soups and sauces
dashi.preparationNotes: Never boil kombu, gently heat to extract umami without bitterness
dashi.technicalTips: Remove kombu before water boils, then add katsuobushi off heat
dashi.storageInstructions: Store refrigerated up to 3 days or freeze up to 1 month

tare.name: Tare
tare.description: Concentrated seasoning sauce used as a flavoring base for many Japanese dishes
tare.preparationNotes: Often simmered with aromatics like ginger, garlic, and scallions
tare.technicalTips: Balance sweet, salty, and umami carefully; adjust with kombu or bonito

shoyu.name: Shoyu (Soy Sauce)
shoyu.description: Fermented soybean sauce that forms the foundation of Japanese cuisine
shoyu.preparationNotes: Traditional brewing takes months of fermentation
shoyu.technicalTips: Different shoyu types are suited for different applications, usukuchi is lighter and saltier

miso.name: Miso
miso.description: Fermented soybean paste with complex umami flavor
miso.preparationNotes: Fermentation period determines color and flavor intensity
miso.technicalTips: Never boil miso to preserve live cultures and flavor complexity

ponzu.name: Ponzu
ponzu.description: Tangy citrus-based sauce with soy and dashi
ponzu.preparationNotes: Best when aged for several days to develop flavor

mentsuyu.name: Mentsuyu
mentsuyu.description: Multipurpose noodle soup base and seasoning sauce
mentsuyu.preparationNotes: Can be prepared concentrated and diluted as needed

teriyaki.name: Teriyaki
teriyaki.description: Sweet-savory glaze with soy sauce, mirin, and sugar
teriyaki.preparationNotes: Traditionally applied in layers while grilling

regionalCuisines.name: Kansai/Kyoto Cuisine
regionalCuisines.description: Refined, delicate flavors emphasizing natural taste of ingredients with minimal seasoning

regionalCuisines.name: Kanto/Tokyo Cuisine
regionalCuisines.description: Bolder, more soy-focused flavors with urban innovations

regionalCuisines.name: Hokkaido Cuisine
regionalCuisines.description: Hearty, dairy-influenced northern cuisine with abundant seafood

astrologicalInfluences: Neptune - Governs the subtle dashi broths and seafood elements
Mercury - Influences the precision and attention to detail
Moon - Shapes the cyclical nature of seasonal cuisine

Korean.name: Korean
Korean.description: Bold flavors from fermentation and grilling.

gochujang.name: Gochujang
gochujang.description: Fermented red chili paste with sweet, savory, and spicy notes
gochujang.preparationNotes: Traditionally fermented for months in earthenware pots called onggi
gochujang.technicalTips: Balance with sweeteners like honey or sugar to mellow its intensity

doenjang.name: Doenjang
doenjang.description: Fermented soybean paste with rich umami flavor and earthy notes
doenjang.preparationNotes: Traditionally separated from soy sauce during fermentation of meju
doenjang.technicalTips: Add at the beginning of cooking to develop depth of flavor

ssamjang.name: Ssamjang
ssamjang.description: Thick, spicy dipping sauce for wrapped meat and vegetables
ssamjang.preparationNotes: Mix ingredients fresh before serving for best flavor
ssamjang.technicalTips: Balance sweet, savory, and spicy elements to complement the main dish

ganjang.name: Ganjang (Korean Soy Sauce)
ganjang.description: Traditional Korean soy sauce, often more complex than Chinese or Japanese varieties
ganjang.preparationNotes: Traditionally separated from doenjang during fermentation
ganjang.technicalTips: Use premium varieties for dipping sauces and everyday ones for cooking

chogochujang.name: Chogochujang
chogochujang.description: Sweet and sour chili sauce with vinegar
chogochujang.preparationNotes: Best made fresh rather than stored long-term
chogochujang.technicalTips: Adjust vinegar and sugar ratio to complement the dish being served

yangnyeom.name: Yangnyeom Sauce
yangnyeom.description: Sweet and spicy sauce used for Korean fried chicken and other dishes
yangnyeom.preparationNotes: Mix thoroughly and cook briefly to develop flavors
yangnyeom.technicalTips: The sauce should coat the back of a spoon but still be pourable

bulgogi.name: Bulgogi Marinade
bulgogi.description: Sweet and savory marinade for grilled beef and other meats
bulgogi.preparationNotes: Asian pear helps tenderize meat while adding subtle sweetness
bulgogi.technicalTips: Marinate beef for at least 2 hours, preferably overnight for best flavor penetration

sesameOil.name: Chamgireum (Sesame Oil Dressing)
sesameOil.description: Aromatic oil-based dressing used for many Korean dishes
sesameOil.preparationNotes: Use high-quality freshly toasted sesame oil for best flavor
sesameOil.technicalTips: Add at the end of cooking to preserve volatile aromatics

regionalCuisines.name: Seoul (Capital) Cuisine
regionalCuisines.description: Refined, royal-influenced cuisine with balanced flavors

regionalCuisines.name: Jeonju (Southwest) Cuisine
regionalCuisines.description: Known as Korea's food capital, with emphasis on quality ingredients and tradition

regionalCuisines.name: Gyeongsang (Southeast) Cuisine
regionalCuisines.description: Bold, spicy flavors with substantial seafood influence

regionalCuisines.name: Jeju Island Cuisine
regionalCuisines.description: Unique island cuisine with distinctive ingredients like black pork and abalone

Mexican.name: Mexican
Mexican.description: Vibrant flavors with a focus on chilies, corn, and traditional salsas.

mole.name: Mole
mole.description: Complex sauce combining chiles, spices, nuts, and chocolate
mole.preparationNotes: Traditionally prepared over multiple days for celebrations and special occasions
mole.technicalTips: Toast ingredients separately to develop maximum flavor complexity

salsaVerde.name: Salsa Verde
salsaVerde.description: Tangy green sauce made from tomatillos, chiles, and herbs
salsaVerde.preparationNotes: Can be served raw or cooked depending on desired flavor profile
salsaVerde.technicalTips: Roasting ingredients before blending adds smoky depth

salsaRoja.name: Salsa Roja
salsaRoja.description: Rich red sauce made from tomatoes and dried chiles
salsaRoja.preparationNotes: Most traditional version uses dried chiles rehydrated and blended with tomatoes
salsaRoja.technicalTips: Straining after blending creates a smoother texture

adobo.name: Adobo
adobo.description: Chile-based marinade with vinegar and spices
adobo.preparationNotes: Originally used as a preservation technique, now primarily for flavor
adobo.technicalTips: Longer marinating creates deeper flavor, but can break down delicate proteins

pipian.name: Pipián
pipian.description: Pre-Hispanic sauce based on ground pumpkin seeds
pipian.preparationNotes: Pre-Hispanic sauce that predates European influence in Mexican cuisine
pipian.technicalTips: Toast seeds until fragrant but not burnt for optimal flavor

regionalCuisines.name: Oaxacan Cuisine
regionalCuisines.description: Known as the 'land of seven moles' with rich indigenous culinary traditions

regionalCuisines.name: Yucatecan Cuisine
regionalCuisines.description: Maya-influenced cuisine with distinctive achiote and citrus flavors

regionalCuisines.name: Northern Cuisine
regionalCuisines.description: Meat-focused cuisine with flour tortillas and grilled specialties

regionalCuisines.name: Central Mexican Cuisine
regionalCuisines.description: Home to Mexico City with ancient Aztec influences and modern street food

regionalCuisines.name: Pacific Coast Cuisine
regionalCuisines.description: Seafood-forward cuisine with tropical fruits and fresh preparations

Middle Eastern.name: Middle Eastern
Middle Eastern.description: Aromatic spices, grains, and grilled meats with fresh vegetable salads.

tahini.name: Tahini
tahini.description: Creamy sesame seed paste used as a base for many Middle Eastern sauces
tahini.preparationNotes: Traditionally ground with stone mills to preserve flavor and nutrients
tahini.technicalTips: Stir well before using as natural separation occurs. Add water slowly when thinning

hummus.name: Hummus
hummus.description: Creamy chickpea dip with tahini, garlic, and lemon
hummus.preparationNotes: Each region claims to make the most authentic version. Texture can range from rustic to silky smooth
hummus.technicalTips: Cook chickpeas with baking soda to help break down skins for smoother texture

zaatar.name: Za'atar Oil
zaatar.description: Herb and sesame blend mixed with olive oil for dipping and spreading
zaatar.seasonality: all, with fresh variations in spring
zaatar.preparationNotes: Family recipes are closely guarded secrets, with regional variations in proportions
zaatar.technicalTips: Mix with high-quality olive oil just before serving to preserve aromatics

harissa.name: Harissa
harissa.description: Hot chile paste with garlic, spices, and olive oil
harissa.preparationNotes: Traditional preservation technique for chiles in North African cuisine
harissa.technicalTips: A little goes a long way. Store with a layer of olive oil on top to preserve freshness

toum.name: Toum
toum.description: Intense garlic sauce with an airy, creamy texture
toum.preparationNotes: Traditionally made by hand pounding in a mortar and pestle until emulsified
toum.technicalTips: Slow oil incorporation is essential for proper emulsification and fluffy texture

regionalCuisines.name: Levantine Cuisine
regionalCuisines.description: Cuisine of the Eastern Mediterranean coast, featuring olive oil, herbs, and za'atar

regionalCuisines.name: Persian Cuisine
regionalCuisines.description: Ancient Iranian culinary tradition with complex rice dishes and delicate use of herbs and fruits

regionalCuisines.name: North African Cuisine
regionalCuisines.description: Bold, spicy flavors with influences from Berber, Arab, Mediterranean, and Sub-Saharan traditions

regionalCuisines.name: Arabian Peninsula Cuisine
regionalCuisines.description: Desert-adapted cuisine with dates, rice, camel products, and distinctive spice blends

regionalCuisines.name: Turkish-Influenced Cuisine
regionalCuisines.description: Ottoman culinary legacy with layered flavors, yogurt, and regional variations

Russian.name: Russian
Russian.description: Hearty soups, grains, and preserved foods suitable for cold climates.

smetana.name: Smetana
smetana.description: Cultured sour cream with rich texture and tangy flavor
smetana.preparationNotes: Traditionally fermented at room temperature for 24-48 hours to develop flavor and texture
smetana.technicalTips: Use as a finishing touch, adding after cooking to preserve its probiotic properties

adjika.name: Adjika
adjika.description: Spicy pepper and herb paste from the Caucasus region
adjika.preparationNotes: Traditionally ground with stone mortar and pestle, then fermented in clay pots
adjika.technicalTips: Can be used raw or cooked intensity mellows with cooking

khrenovina.name: Khrenovina
khrenovina.preparationNotes: Often prepared during harvest season when horseradish is at its most pungent
khrenovina.technicalTips: Grate horseradish in well-ventilated area or underwater to prevent eye irritation

gribnoj_soys.name: Gribnoj Sous
gribnoj_soys.description: Rich mushroom sauce with sour cream base
gribnoj_soys.seasonality: autumn mushroom harvest, preserved for year-round use
gribnoj_soys.preparationNotes: Traditionally made with foraged wild mushrooms dried mushrooms are reconstituted in winter
gribnoj_soys.technicalTips: Brown mushrooms thoroughly to develop full umami flavor before adding liquids

ikra.name: Ikra Baklazhanaya
ikra.seasonality: summer preparation, preserved for winter use
ikra.preparationNotes: Traditional preparation involves roasting eggplants over open flame for smoky flavor
ikra.technicalTips: Let flavors marry overnight for best taste, serve at room temperature

regionalCuisines.name: Northern Russian Cuisine
regionalCuisines.description: Fish-forward cuisine with berries, mushrooms, and hearty grains adapted to cold climate

regionalCuisines.name: Central Russian Cuisine
regionalCuisines.description: Classic Russian dishes with simple ingredients and traditional cooking methods

regionalCuisines.name: Siberian Cuisine
regionalCuisines.description: Hearty, calorie-rich food designed for extreme cold, featuring game and wild plants

regionalCuisines.name: Caucasian-Influenced Russian Cuisine
regionalCuisines.description: Southern Russian cooking with strong influences from Georgia, Armenia, and Azerbaijan

regionalCuisines.name: Volga Region Cuisine
regionalCuisines.description: Diverse cuisine reflecting the multicultural Volga river basin with Tatar influences

Thai.name: Thai
Thai.description: Perfect balance of sour, sweet, salty, and spicy flavors.

namPlaWaan.name: Nam Pla Wan (Sweet Fish Sauce)
namPlaWaan.description: Sweet, spicy, and salty sauce combining fish sauce with palm sugar and chili
namPlaWaan.preparationNotes: Balance is key - should achieve equal sweet, sour, and salty notes with heat according to preference
namPlaWaan.technicalTips: Palm sugar can be melted with a little water to help it dissolve more easily

namPhrik.name: Nam Phrik (Chili Paste)
namPhrik.description: Foundation of Thai cuisine, a versatile chili-based paste with regional variations
namPhrik.preparationNotes: Traditional preparation involves pounding in a mortar and pestle to develop complex flavors
namPhrik.technicalTips: Roasting ingredients before pounding enhances aroma and reduces raw spiciness

padThaiSauce.name: Pad Thai Sauce
padThaiSauce.description: Sweet-sour-salty sauce that defines Thailand's most famous noodle dish
padThaiSauce.preparationNotes: Balance of sour from tamarind, sweet from palm sugar, and salty from fish sauce is crucial
padThaiSauce.technicalTips: Prepare in advance and reduce to concentrate flavors before adding to noodles

currySauces.name: Curry Pastes/Sauces
currySauces.description: Aromatic spice and herb pastes that form the foundation of Thai curries
currySauces.preparationNotes: Traditional preparation requires significant time pounding ingredients to release oils and flavor compounds
currySauces.technicalTips: Fry paste in coconut cream (the thick part that rises to the top of coconut milk) until aromatic and oil separates

srirachaSauce.name: Sriracha Sauce
srirachaSauce.description: Fermented chili sauce with garlic and vinegar that has gained worldwide popularity
srirachaSauce.preparationNotes: Traditional Thai version is tangier and thinner than the popular American version
srirachaSauce.technicalTips: Fermentation develops depth of flavor beyond simple chili heat

regionalCuisines.name: Northern Thai (Lanna)
regionalCuisines.description: More mild and less spicy cuisine with Burmese and Lao influences, featuring sticky rice and pork

regionalCuisines.name: Northeastern Thai (Isaan)
regionalCuisines.description: Intense flavors with Lao influence, featuring fermentation, spicy chilies, and sticky rice

regionalCuisines.name: Central Thai
regionalCuisines.description: The royal court cuisine with balanced flavors combining sweet, sour, salty, and spicy elements

regionalCuisines.name: Southern Thai
regionalCuisines.description: Intensely spicy and aromatic cuisine with Malaysian influences and abundant seafood

regionalCuisines.name: Royal Thai Cuisine
regionalCuisines.description: Refined, artistic cuisine developed in the royal palace with intricate preparation techniques

Vietnamese.name: Vietnamese
Vietnamese.description: Fresh, light flavors with an emphasis on herbs and clear broths.

nuocCham.name: Nước Chấm
nuocCham.description: Quintessential Vietnamese dipping sauce combining fish sauce, lime, sugar, and chili
nuocCham.preparationNotes: Balance is critical - should harmonize sweet, sour, salty, and spicy flavors in perfect proportion
nuocCham.technicalTips: Let sit for at least 15 minutes before serving to allow flavors to meld

nuocMam.name: Nước Mắm (Fish Sauce)
nuocMam.description: Fermented anchovy sauce that forms the foundation of Vietnamese cuisine
nuocMam.preparationNotes: Traditional production takes at least 12 months of fermentation in wooden barrels
nuocMam.technicalTips: High-quality fish sauce should have a deep amber color and complex aroma beyond just fishiness

tuongOt.name: Tương Ớt (Chili Sauce)
tuongOt.description: Vietnamese-style fermented chili sauce with garlic and vinegar
tuongOt.preparationNotes: Traditional recipes often include fermentation to develop deeper flavor
tuongOt.technicalTips: Roasting or charring chilies first adds complexity and tempers raw heat

tuongDen.name: Tương Đen (Black Bean Sauce)
tuongDen.description: Fermented soybean sauce used in Vietnamese-Chinese fusion dishes
tuongDen.preparationNotes: Often used in dishes showing Chinese culinary influence in Vietnamese cuisine
tuongDen.technicalTips: Toast in oil before using to release aromatics and reduce raw bean flavor

saTe.name: Sa Tế (Vietnamese Sateay Sauce)
saTe.description: Aromatic lemongrass and chili paste used in soups and stir-fries
saTe.preparationNotes: Most authentic when chilies and aromatics are pounded by hand in a mortar and pestle
saTe.technicalTips: The oil should separate when fried properly, creating a vibrant red layer on top

regionalCuisines.name: Northern Vietnamese
regionalCuisines.description: More subtle and delicate flavors with Chinese influence and less spice and sugar

regionalCuisines.name: Central Vietnamese
regionalCuisines.description: Bold, spicy flavors influenced by royal cuisine with elaborate presentation

regionalCuisines.name: Southern Vietnamese
regionalCuisines.description: Sweet, vibrant flavors with abundant fresh herbs and tropical ingredients

regionalCuisines.name: Mekong Delta
regionalCuisines.description: Emphasizes freshwater fish, tropical fruits, and rice with Khmer influences

regionalCuisines.name: Highland Vietnamese
regionalCuisines.description: Rustic, earthy cuisine utilizing mountain ingredients and ethnic minority traditions

Fusion.name: Fusion
Fusion.description: Innovative culinary intersections bridging traditions across cultures through elemental harmony.

sambalRomesco.name: Sambal Romesco
sambalRomesco.description: Catalan roasted red pepper and toasted almond romesco invigorated with fiery fermented Indonesian sambal oelek and lime zest.
sambalRomesco.base: Roasted red peppers and crushed nuts
sambalRomesco.thickener: Toasted Marcona almonds and stale rustic bread
sambalRomesco.preparationNotes: Blend toasted almonds with garlic and vinegar first before streaming in oil for a creamy emulsion.
sambalRomesco.technicalTips: Toast the nuts deeply for earthy undertones to balance the bright chili fire.
sambalRomesco.storageInstructions: Refrigerate up to 7 days in airtight glass jar.

misoBechamel.name: Miso Béchamel
misoBechamel.description: French classical white roux and infused whole milk enriched with sweet, umami-dense Japanese shiro miso and white pepper.
misoBechamel.preparationNotes: Dissolve miso in a ladle of warm milk before whisking into the finished béchamel to avoid graininess.
misoBechamel.technicalTips: Do not let the roux brown; keep it pale white to preserve delicate sweetness.
misoBechamel.storageInstructions: Refrigerate up to 4 days; reheat gently over low heat whisking in splash of milk.

ponzuChimichurri.name: Ponzu Chimichurri
ponzuChimichurri.description: Argentine fresh parsley, oregano, and garlic vinaigrette brightened with Japanese yuzu ponzu and sesame oil.
ponzuChimichurri.base: Extra-virgin olive oil and yuzu ponzu
ponzuChimichurri.preparationNotes: Always chop herbs by hand — food processors bruise herbs and release bitter moisture.
ponzuChimichurri.technicalTips: Rest the sauce for 30 minutes before serving so flavors bloom into the oil.
ponzuChimichurri.storageInstructions: Store refrigerated up to 5 days. Bring to room temp before serving.
